analyst_view.overall: Betis are 4th with 27 points and strong at home (five wins in six at La Cartuja), while Rayo are 16th with 12 points, have no away win in six and lost 0-1 at home to Valencia last weekend. Betis play in the Champions League in Bratislava on Tuesday night and then host Rayo at 14:00 on Saturday, which is a short turnaround with an early kick-off; the numbers do not add anything for that. Ceballos and Morante are out and the numbers already take them off; new since then, Lo Celso hurt his knee in training on Sunday and missed the Bratislava trip, and his availability for Saturday is unknown (one outlet, FutbolFantasy, has the details). Rayo, under Beñat San José, are without Batalla and Luiz Felipe (counted), with Óscar Valentín a doubt. No referee named yet; Betis have not beaten Rayo in the last five meetings, which the numbers count lightly.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals, already a touch lower for Morante and Ceballos being out, Betis's quiet last six games and a run of tight meetings with Rayo. I lean slightly lower again, to about 2.3: Lo Celso, one of Betis's main creators, hurt his knee and is a doubt, and Betis come off a Champions League trip on Tuesday with a 14:00 Saturday kick-off. Rayo have scored only 6 in 6 away games, so most of the goals should come from Betis.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.5 corners, with Betis's recent rise in corners (33 in six) already added. Betis attack wide through Abde and Antony (Antony shook off a knock from the derby) and Rayo push full-backs forward, so a normal corner count fits. Nothing I found changes this, so I stay at 10.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.4 cards, with Rayo expected to take most of them; their recent card counts and the meetings between these sides are already counted. The referee has not been named yet, so his record can't be judged until later in the week. Rayo away from home, chasing points near the bottom, usually defend a lot and foul, which the numbers already reflect, so I stay at 5.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.6 shots, pushed up by strong recent shot counts on both sides (Rayo 104 in their last six), which the numbers already add. I lean a little lower, to about 30.3: Betis play in Bratislava on Tuesday night, may rotate for an early Saturday kick-off, and could lack Lo Celso, who sets up many of their chances. In the derby on Saturday Betis produced their lowest expected goals of the league season.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.5 shots on target, with recent form and the missing Ceballos already counted. I trim it slightly, to about 9.2, for the same reasons as shots: a midweek Champions League trip, the early kick-off and Lo Celso's knee problem. Rayo's finishing away has been weak, which the numbers already know.
